daily.title: Mint Money Festival | Indians should invest up to 40% capital abroad, says Devina Mehra
daily.summary: Devina Mehra challenges the view that geopolitical conflicts cause lasting equity market downturns, citing historical market returns spanning more than a century. Indian investors should allocate up to 40% of their portfolios to international markets to offset currency depreciation and reduce concentration risk, according to Devina Mehra, founder, chairperson and managing director of First Global. “I would say that you have at least 30-40% of your portfolio globally,” she said in a fireside chat at the Mint Money Festival 2026, in Mumbai on Saturday.

daily.title: Why your gold loan terms may get tougher: Lenders demand extra collateral as bullion prices fall and repayments slip
daily.summary: When gold prices fall, a loan can slip above its permitted LTV limit. To bring it back in line, lenders are asking borrowers to pledge more gold or repay part of the outstanding amount.

daily.title: Section 69A Addition Unsustainable Where Cash Deposits Are Supported by Evidence: ITAT Agra
daily.summary: Agra ITAT deletes ₹20.36 lakh cash deposit addition under Section 69A after accepting bank statements, affidavits and agricultural land records. The Agra ITAT deleted an addition of ₹20,36,500 under section 69A after accepting the assessee’s explanation for cash deposited in his bank account. The Tribunal found that bank statements corroborated the movement of ₹15 lakh connected with a cancelled land purchase and that affidavits, identity documents and agricultural land records supported the explanation for a further ₹5 lakh cash receipt . The Revenue brought no adverse material to rebut that evidence.

daily.title: CBDT Introduces New Form 180A for New Development Bank to Claim Income Tax Exemption under Schedule VII
daily.summary: CBDT introduces a new Form 180A for the New Development Bank to furnish information for claiming income tax exemption, along with prescribed filing and verification requirements. The Central Board of Direct Taxes ( CBDT ) under the Ministry of Finance (Department of Revenue), vide Notification No. G.S.R. 1011(E), dated November 27, 2026 , has amended the Income-tax Rules, 2026, by introducing a new Form No. 180A. The amended rules will now be known as the Income-tax (Ninth Amendment) Rules, 2026 , effective from November 27, 2026.

daily.title: Section 148 Notice Beyond Three Years Needs Section 151(ii) Approval: ITAT Delhi
daily.summary: ITAT Delhi quashes AY 2016-17 reassessment as the fresh Section 148 notice issued beyond three years lacked valid approval under Section 151(ii). Summary: The Delhi ITAT held that a fresh notice under section 148 , issued on 29 July 2022 for AY 2016–17 , required approval from the authority specified in section 151(ii) . More than three years had elapsed from the end of the relevant assessment year, and the Principal Commissioner of Income Tax (PCIT) had approved the notice under section 151(i) .

For AY 2016–17 , the assessee filed a return declaring total income of ₹7,77,200 and agricultural income of ₹7,43,000 . The return was initially processed under section 143(1) . The case was subsequently selected for complete scrutiny, and the Assessing Officer issued notices under sections 143(2) and 142(1) . The Assessing Officer recorded that the assessee had not furnished the required details of agricultural income and corresponding expenditure.

daily.title: Section 271DA Penalty Limitation Runs From Assessment Order Initiation: ITAT Delhi
daily.summary: ITAT Delhi deletes Rs. 23.02 lakh Section 271DA penalty, holding that limitation under Section 275(1)(c) begins from AO’s recorded satisfaction. Summary: The Delhi ITAT deleted a ₹23,02,500 penalty under section 271DA because the Additional Commissioner passed the penalty order after the limitation period under section 275(1)(c) had expired. The Assessing Officer had recorded his satisfaction in the assessment order dated 19 January 2024 that a reference would be made for penalty proceedings for an alleged violation of section 269ST . The Tribunal treated that recording as the initiation of penalty action.

daily.title: Cash Transaction Limit: RBI New Money Transfer Rules 2026
daily.summary: RBI's Domestic Money Transfer Directions, 2026 prescribe cash transaction limits, including ₹10,000 per cash payout, ₹5,000 per cash deposit through BCs and ATMs, and ₹50,000 NEFT transfers at bank branches, along with enhanced KYC and authentication requirements. While the Directions have been presented as RBI's new Domestic Money Transfer framework, many of the transaction limits remain unchanged. The primary objective of the Directions is to consolidate existing instructions, strengthen customer protection measures and enhance operational safeguards.

breaking.summary: State-owned Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL) has approved an investment of Rs 1,26,656 crore, with an estimated cost variation of 20 per cent, to set up an integrated greenfield refinery and petrochemical complex at Ramayapatnam in Andhra Pradesh, marking a major expansion of its refining and petrochemical footprint.
